svg.title: After summing labels and dividing by the occurrence factorial (m!), its contribution is at most eδcB(Y )tm Q j kj!/m!. All child factorials are paid together by an exact parent-map count. For maps from m numbered objects into r bins, let Am(r) be the sum of the products of their bin-size factorials. Appending one object to bin j multiplies the weight by kj + 1; summing over bins gives (m+r). Hence A0(r) = 1 and Am+1(r) = (m + r)Am(r). With r = m + 1,
